title: [dynamo] empty FX graph generated on graph break
bug_description:
Consider this code:
```python
import torch


@torch.compile(backend="eager")
def fn(x, i):
    if i == 1:
        torch._dynamo.graph_break()
    return x + 1


inp = torch.randn(3)
fn(inp, 0)
fn(inp, 1)
fn(inp, 2)
```

which generates graphs:
```

 /data/users/williamwen/pytorch3/torch/fx/_lazy_graph_module.py class GraphModule(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(self, L_x_: "f32[3][1]cpu"):
        l_x_ = L_x_
        
         # File: /data/users/williamwen/pytorch3/playground3.py:8 in fn, code: return x + 1
        add: "f32[3][1]cpu" = l_x_ + 1;  l_x_ = None
        return (add,)

 ===== __compiled_fn_4_7b89acc6_24c3_4d27_b288_55c865735053 =====
 /data/users/williamwen/pytorch3/torch/fx/_lazy_graph_module.py class GraphModule(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(self):
        return ()

    def forward(self, L_x_: "f32[3][1]cpu"):
        l_x_ = L_x_
        
         # File: /data/users/williamwen/pytorch3/playground3.py:8 in torch_dynamo_resume_in_fn_at_7, code: return x + 1
        add: "f32[3][1]cpu" = l_x_ + 1;  l_x_ = None
        return (add,)
        

TRACED GRAPH
 ===== __compiled_fn_9_b21379e5_8d71_4e7f_81ca_1d019102cb18 =====
 /data/users/williamwen/pytorch3/torch/fx/_lazy_graph_module.py class GraphModule(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(self, L_x_: "f32[3][1]cpu"):
        l_x_ = L_x_
        
         # File: /data/users/williamwen/pytorch3/playground3.py:8 in fn, code: return x + 1
        add: "f32[3][1]cpu" = l_x_ + 1;  l_x_ = None
        return (add,)
```

Perhaps we don't wish to actually compile the 2nd graph, which is empty. We already have logic in `output_graph.py` that doesn't compile empty graphs, but this case seems to slip through the cracks since in the second graph, there is a check for `i == 1` that gets pruned from the graph.

This could be as simple as adding an exit from `compile_and_call_fx_graph`, but I haven't checked if this breaks other things yet.
